title: RTLFixer: Automatically Fixing RTL Syntax Errors with Large Language Model
problem: Approximately 55% of errors in LLM-generated Verilog code are syntax-related, causing compilation failures. This severely limits the practical applicability of LLMs for automatic hardware design generation.
motivation: As LLMs are increasingly used for hardware code generation, automatic correction of syntax errors is critical to improve code quality and reduce manual debugging effort.
method: RTLFixer employs Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and ReAct prompting to enable LLMs to act as autonomous debugging agents. The framework interactively debugs Verilog code by receiving compilation feedback and iteratively correcting syntax errors through multiple reasoning steps, achieving 98.5% correction rate on 212 erroneous implementations.
key_novelty: Using RAG and ReAct prompting to enable autonomous interactive debugging where LLMs iteratively fix Verilog syntax errors based on compiler feedback.
contributions: Framework for autonomous syntax error fixing in Verilog using LLMs with RAG and ReAct prompting
Achieves 98.5% compilation error correction rate on 212 erroneous Verilog implementations from VerilogEval
Improves pass@1 success rates by 32.3% on VerilogEval-Machine and 10.1% on VerilogEval-Human benchmarks
Open-sourced code and benchmark dataset for reproducibility

metrics.accuracy: 98.5% syntax error correction rate; +32.3% pass@1 on VerilogEval-Machine; +10.1% pass@1 on VerilogEval-Human
